memory_update.text: LRN is the direct pure-play anchor for the k12_virtual_career_pathways node: virtual/blended public schools plus General Education and Career Learning school-as-a-service.
PSO is a diversified but important virtual-school competitor/supplier through Pearson Virtual Schools and Connections Academy; isolate Virtual Learning economics before ranking.
NRDY is a direct tutoring/remediation candidate but below USD 1B and exposed to district/federal/state funding delays; include as high-relevance, high-risk exception.
COUR may be an underappreciated career-pathways/credential supplier for high schools, but current evidence is case-study level rather than disclosed K-12 revenue scale.
KLTR is a second-order virtual-classroom infrastructure supplier; include only as a supplier hypothesis until K-12 customer concentration or named district/operator relationships are verified.

Many important K-12 assessment/curriculum/tutoring vendors are private or recently taken private, including PowerSchool, Renaissance, IXL, Edmentum, Newsela, and HMH; public-market coverage is therefore incomplete.

For this node, the key chokepoint appears to be public-sector authorization, charter/district contract durability, funding continuity, and outcomes credibility rather than generic digital curriculum supply.

node: K-12 virtual schooling, tutoring, credit recovery, and career/technical pathways
summary: Expanded universe for the K-12 virtual schooling and career-pathway node. The clearest direct public-market mappings are Stride and Pearson through full-time virtual public-school operations and K-12 virtual-school platforms. Less obvious second-order or adjacent candidates include Nerdy for district-facing high-dosage tutoring, Coursera for high-school career credentials and credit-recovery/workforce pathways, and Kaltura as a virtual-classroom/video infrastructure supplier to education institutions. Several below-USD-1B names are included as exceptions because their node relevance is unusually direct, but their scale/liquidity and business durability require extra verification.
